findings.reason: a node that implements only the server-mode gate enables the signal rerank on every full server, bypassing the measurement decision the done-when exists to enforce.
findings.text: §7 states "The switch follows the DD-path rerank: on for a full or facility server, off for a read-only or DD-only server", which is the server-mode-derived `_rerank_dd_paths = not (read_only or dd_only)` (imas_codex/llm/server.py:1882), yet its done-when (line 351) says the switch "ships on only if" the measurement supports it and node 2 "leaves it off"; a node cannot tell whether one switch is reused or whether a second flag gates §7's rerank

findings.reason: §1 is a historical account of the pre-§4 state whose mechanism §4 has already replaced, so the stale line numbers mislead a curious reader but change no node's work.

findings.reason: fusion is an explicit comparator and the decision rule can fail, so the node can show its guard bites without a separate mutation control.
findings.text: §7's done-when is a decision rule (rerank must beat fusion on mean nDCG@10 and grade-3 precision@5 over three passes, p95 within 5 s) but names no declared negative control, unlike §4 ("The old rule must fail the same test") and §8 (a control query whose top 5 holds a grade-2 reference)

findings.text: §7's third node both "scores the arms and decides the switch" and "ports the §4 and §5 measurement scripts into that module", two deliverables that cannot be closed on one verdict
